_comment: Hand-curated seed knowledge graph: symptom -> remedy (parameter move) -> side-effect symptoms. Grow it from docs and from your own run logs (docs/ROADMAP.md M5). Every edge should be defensible from a primary source; 'evidence' names the document family, verify the exact section before citing it.

memory_bound.detect: arithmetic intensity under the tiling is below the roofline ridge

low_ilp.detect: micro-tile TM*TN < 16: too few FMAs per shared-memory load

underfilled_gpu.detect: fewer than one full wave of thread blocks

remedies.why: Accumulators dominate register use (TM*TN). Under __launch_bounds__ the compiler caps registers at regs_per_SM/threads, so large micro-tiles with many threads spill to local memory.
remedies.evidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide: launch bounds; Best Practices Guide: register pressure

remedies.why: Same as r1, along the other micro-tile dimension.
remedies.evidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide: launch bounds

remedies.why: Fewer threads per block raises the per-thread register cap.
Fewer registers per thread lets more blocks co-reside on an SM, hiding shared/global latency.
Shared memory per block is BK*(BM+PAD+BN)*4 bytes; shrinking BK lets more blocks fit when shared memory is the occupancy limiter.
Global traffic scales as MNK*(1/BM + 1/BN). Larger block tiles raise arithmetic intensity toward the ridge point.
remedies.evidence: Roofline model (Williams et al.); tiled GEMM analysis

remedies.why: Padding rows of the transposed A tile by the amount the bank model selects de-aliases the 32 banks (see compiler/include/PtxForge/BankModel.h).
remedies.evidence: CUDA Best Practices Guide: shared memory bank conflicts

remedies.why: A TMxTN micro-tile does TM*TN FMAs for TM+TN shared loads; bigger tiles amortize loads.
Fewer than one wave of blocks leaves SMs idle; smaller tiles create more blocks.
